messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] [rsiena-help][5137] problem in running my model
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jia,

The message indicates that the simulation process cannot terminate. This 
could be because the rate parameter has been made so large the steps 
happen too frequently or because the network cannot make any more changes.

If you cannot work out what has happened, give me a bit more information: 
are you using the siena01Gui, or the command line interface, which version 
of RSiena, R,... Then I can tailor my advice as to the next step.

Regards

Ruth

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] crash during estimation of bipartite behaviour model
messages.subject_clean: [Rsiena-help] crash during estimation of bipartite behaviour model
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

while running siena07 (RSiena rev=184 on a multi-core Linux-based machine)
to estimate a coevolution network/behaviour model using bipartite networks,
I encountered the following problem:

I specified the model with a dependent bipartite network (4 sparse
matrices, 135x719 nodes), a bunch of strucural (cycle4, outActSqrt,
inPopSqrt, outInAss) and individual covariates, a dependent behavioural
variable (related to the first nodeset), and a bunch of behavioural
parameters (avSim and outdegree, plus of course the defaults linear and
quadratic shape). Then I launched siena07 and I was able to get through
phase1, until this error message popped up:

Error in if (dfra[i, i] < 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

Can you please help me on this?

Thanks a lot.
Marco

messages.subject_clean: [Rsiena-help] crash during estimation of bipartite behaviour model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Marco.

I'll throw out a guess. The dfra object is probably the initial derivative
estimate. If a value in the matrix is missing, I guess it means the partial
derivative could not be estimated. Maybe this is because of something funny
in your covariate coding. Perhaps the first thing to do is look for errors
in your data. I could also imagine that a lack of variability in a
covariate could cause some issues.

Good luck. I hope some more informed guesses will emerge.

Nathan Doogan

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] crash during estimation of bipartite behaviour model
messages.subject_clean: [Rsiena-help] crash during estimation of bipartite behaviour model
messages.body_plain:
Marco,

Yes, the message is from the routine trying to calculate the derivative 
matrix. The error usually arises due to problems with the data. Clues to 
the cause may appear in reports on the data, or messages during the run. 
It might be worth checking the file cluster.out where sub processes will 
write messages.

If you can run a model with no effects other than the defaults  the the 
problem could be due to collinearity in effects.

If you cannot figure it out, and want me to look at the data, please 
sent it to me direct.

Regards,

Ruth
